name: my-webserver
description: my-webserver — local file server with Markdown, JSON/YAML table, and Eruda DevTools rendering. Ships as a prebuilt, per-arch Node Single Executable Application binary.

build._remote_note: The Node Single Executable Application build (node --experimental-sea-config + postject injection, both architectures) is heavy and fragile across environments — built on GHA (ship-my-webserver-app.yml), published to the rolling GitHub Release, and fetched by the desktop and Termux nix modules. Never built locally.
build._release_tag_note: A PREFIX, not a tag. ship-my-webserver-app.yml appends the publishing commit's short sha, so every publish lands on a tag that is created once and never rewritten. The tag used to be the rolling my-webserver-latest, clobbered on every upload: a fixed-output derivation pins a hash, which is a promise the bytes at that URL never change, and a clobbered tag breaks that promise for every consumer already holding the old hash. See nix/hashes.json's tag field, which is what the fetch actually reads.

android_abi._doc: What makes a published binary RUNNABLE ON ANDROID, as data rather than as folklore. The per-arch binaries this project ships are built on the official nodejs.org Linux tarball, which is GLIBC: PT_INTERP=/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 and DT_NEEDED against libc.so.6/libstdc++.so.6. Android is bionic. It has no /lib, no libc.so.6 and no ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, and /lib lives on the read-only system partition so no APK can supply one. execve() of such a file returns ENOENT NAMING THE BINARY, not the missing interpreter, which is why this reads as a packaging fault and sends people back to re-checking extractNativeLibs. The aarch64 binary runs under Nix-on-Droid only because proot supplies a glibc root filesystem: the terminal is not the launcher there, it is the runtime. test-android-abi.sh reads this block; nothing about the rule is written in the script.
android_abi._doc_allowed_needed: Resolvable on a stock device (bionic + NDK) or shippable in jniLibs. A DT_NEEDED name is only extractable to nativeLibraryDir if it matches lib*.so, which is PackageManager's own filter, so a versioned soname such as libz.so.1 or libicuuc.so.78 is NOT shippable and must not appear here.

fixtures._doc: A guard only ever observed passing proves nothing, so the self-test runs against two REAL published artifacts with known, opposite answers. Only the first 64 KiB of each is fetched: the ELF header and the program headers, which is where PT_INTERP lives, are at the front of the file.

must_fail.reason: This project's own aarch64 SEA. glibc-linked, so it cannot start on Android. Pinned to an immutable per-commit tag so the fixture cannot drift out from under the test.

must_pass.reason: my-watchdog's aarch64 build: static, no PT_INTERP, no DT_NEEDED. This is the ONE shape in the fleet already proven to exec from nativeLibraryDir on the phone: ac_c3-watchdog ships and runs it today.
